summary.text: A 60-year-old woman was in a traffic accident while walking, was in a coma and was taken to a nearby hospital, then shifted to the authors hospital after 2 weeks. On presentation she was conscious, oriented and hemodynamically stable. Radiographs showed ipsilateral left femoral neck (Garden II, nondisplaced) and sub-trochanteric (Seinsheimer IIIB) fractures and a right ulna olecranon fracture, with AIS 14 and ISS 27.

The sub-trochanteric fracture was treated with a long Gamma3 nail and ORIF, and the femoral neck fracture with closed reduction under fluoroscopy, with screw threads crossing the fracture lines and compression at the femoral neck. At 12-month follow-up the fracture was united with no evidence of avascular necrosis.

At 4-year follow-up the patient began to complain of pain. An X-ray showed evidence of necrosis of the femoral head; the Abstract and the case text give different times for the necrosis. One year after that X-ray she had a total hip arthroplasty for the severe pain.

ambiguities.issue: Source conflict on necrosis timing: the Abstract places evidence of necrosis "after 5 years", while the Case presentation (4-year follow-up), the Fig. 4 caption ("At 4 year follow-up") and the Discussion ("4 year postoperation") place it at 4 years, with arthroplasty one year after the X-ray. All timed necrosis statements are review_only; the untimed necrosis and X-ray result are kept.
